findings.statement: the engine's durable load clears the brief's registered P-A gate of 600k ops/s
findings.detail: supdb loads 758581 ops/s durably at batch 1000 (295.8 MB to the device, 164.1 MB on disk for 110.6 MB of records). The promise registered before this engine existed was >= 600,000 -- within 1.7x of f39's raw+index floor and past LMDB's recorded 572,416; a miss is a design leak to name, not a number to accept

findings.statement: sealing on the committing thread costs a resolvable share of the durable load
findings.detail: supdb-lazyseal 866256 ops/s against supdb 758581 (lazyseal vs supdb: greater 1.142x (p=0.0001, rel_iqr 10.4%/6.8%)): sealing inside the timed window costs 107674 ops/s. Both arms are measured in this process, interleaved, so this is the half of the question the suite can answer

notes: two arms interleaved in one process, a fresh store per rep, the canonical durable load shape. Both commit by WAL append + fdatasync; they differ only in whether a seal can happen inside the timed window (64MB memtable against one that never fills). Device bytes from /proc/self/io per rep; disk bytes are the store's files after close
the gate is the brief's registered P-A: >= 600,000 ops/s, past LMDB's recorded 572,416 (cited as context -- no finding compares across runs)

seal cost 107674 ops/s against a residual of 147747 to f39's raw+index floor (1,014,003, cited from another run and not comparable to this one): the larger names milestone 2, seal off-thread or a cheaper memtable
